contexts.text: The stubborn in their phantasies and cupidities. Signified.
They stubbornly insisted.
They are so stubborn that they never want to desist.
They are the most stubborn of all... AC 5722.
Hell stubbornly insists...
It ought not to be so stubbornly insisted upon. Signified.
When they so stubbornly insisted to come into the Land of Canaan...
(References under Contumacia to passages in which the word Obstinacy occurs.)
They who are so stubborn that they will not suffer themselves to be overcome.
In the other life they are amendable, although they have been stubborn, or had stuck stubbornly to their opinions and falsities.
The punishment is intensified or diminished according to the man's stubbornness and quality.
Obstinacy and stubbornness go for nothing at all: the more stubborn they are, the more grievously do they suffer; for stubbornness must be broken.

Those are the most stubborn of all, who in their life in the world had appeared righteous above others, and were thence in authority, and yet had believed nothing, and had lived a life of self-love...

They who appear to be lying down are more stubborn than all others, and are driven away with difficulty: they have sometimes been with me, and could only be cast out after a lapse of time: the Lord could indeed cast them out in a moment; but it is according to order that their stubbornness should last. For the most part, such have been the greatest adulterers.
See Charles XII here. SE 4745. SE 4748.
The Jews are of such a nature as to stubbornly press on.
The punishments are grievous according to the evil, and frequent according to the stubbornness.
Their stubborn assaults upon charity.
Evil Spirits are stubborn, and take delight in combats... and therefore are not got rid of so...
Such (sorceresses), being the most stubborn of all...
The fight of Jacob with the Angel describes the stubbornness with which they insisted upon possessing the Land of Canaan.
